policy: Fixed fixture contracts for each probe; runners never regenerate these expected values.

provider-contract.invariant: The adapter translates an external language at one boundary.

replace-policy.invariant: A strategy is supplied to the domain operation; the caller can exchange it.

validate-before-side-effect.invariant: The command checks an invariant before invoking its write port.

deduplicate.invariant: Repeated delivery of the same semantic operation has one effect in this store.

commit-intention.invariant: One local transaction preserves both an order and its delivery intention.

compensate.invariant: A compensating credit offsets the prior debit when allocation fails.

version-conflict.invariant: The stale editor cannot silently overwrite a preceding credit.

fence.invariant: The destination compares an ordered generation, including delayed writers.

resource-key.invariant: The shared slot, rather than the caller, is the protected identity.

majority-partition.invariant: Only a partition with two of three members can authorize a new write.

quorum-overlap.invariant: For three replicas, read two and write two have at least one common member.

causal-versions.invariant: A vector exposes concurrent branches before application-specific reconciliation.

logical-clock.invariant: A receive event advances beyond the causal sender clock.

prepared-participant.invariant: A prepared participant cannot invent the coordinator decision.

gossip-membership.invariant: Repeated peer exchanges disseminate membership without a central broadcaster.

stateless-request.invariant: Application instances obtain session state outside local request-process memory, so routing to another instance preserves the request context.

route-enrich-aggregate.invariant: A router chooses a destination; an enricher adds context and an aggregator can count each result.

retry-dlq.invariant: A poison message exhausts three attempts and is retained outside the normal queue.

admission.invariant: Admission limits queued work before consuming unbounded memory.

consumer-topology.invariant: Competing consumers divide work while separate subscriptions each receive the facts they need.

resequence-state.invariant: Sequence metadata enables ordering and a state machine rejects an invalid transition.

retry-budget.invariant: Budgeted attempts, exponential delay and fixed jitter spread work; the open circuit refuses more calls.

dag-dependencies.invariant: A task becomes eligible only after its prerequisites finish.

message-filter.invariant: A filter drops the invalid item while preserving the two valid orders.

message-splitter.invariant: A splitter converts one batch envelope into individual messages and retains their correlation.

cache-key.invariant: Tenant and query scope belong in a key before a cached result is shared.

cache-expiry.invariant: TTL creates an explicit validity boundary and expiration returns control to the producer.

write-policy.invariant: Acknowledging after durable write avoids losing a buffered credit during this crash.

cache-levels.invariant: Invalidation permits the local level to reload from its shared owner.

cache-aside.invariant: A cache-aside miss loads from the source and populates the key; later reads hit that key.

negative-cache.invariant: A known absence is represented by a cached sentinel and suppresses repeated source lookups.

cache-warming.invariant: Preloading a known key moves its initial fetch before the first user read.

replay-events.invariant: An append-only record can replay the credits and debit into a read position.

projection-checkpoint.invariant: A projection advances only after consuming its missing events.

durable-transaction.invariant: A local transaction rolls back an incomplete change while SQLite uses its WAL mode.

snapshot-replay.invariant: A snapshot plus its following events reconstructs the same state with less replay.

shard-route.invariant: A stable key and routing rule direct a lookup to its owning shard.

grain-join.invariant: Aggregating children at the intended grain avoids multiplying the monetary value.

hash-remap.invariant: Adding a modulo shard can move many key owners; a consistent ring aims to limit remapping.

after.query_plan: SEARCH position USING COVERING INDEX position_lookup (account_key=?)

covering-index.invariant: The lookup changes from scanning to an index that includes the selected value.

expand-contract.invariant: Expanding first keeps the old field while the new reader learns the new field.

progressive-route.invariant: A controlled route limits the first new-version population and can redirect it.

shadow-parity.invariant: A shadow computation compares results while the primary owns the user-visible effect.

desired-state.invariant: A reconciler compares declared state with observed state before applying a change.

ab-cohorts.invariant: Both A and B are user-visible treatments assigned to distinct stable cohorts.

object-authorization.invariant: Role, attributes and ownership must be checked against the specific resource.

credential-boundary.invariant: Expiration and audience constrain where and when a credential is accepted.

rotate-key.invariant: Retiring a key makes a credential issued by that key inadmissible to this verifier.

least-network-path.invariant: Explicit allowed edges reduce paths that bypass the application owner.

correlate-retries.invariant: An operation identity relates two request attempts without confusing them.

measure-signals.invariant: Rate, errors and duration expose a slow failed dependency hidden by a vague status.

probe-business-path.invariant: A synthetic business-path check can fail while the process health endpoint stays green.

replica-lag.invariant: An asynchronous replica may serve an older committed value and converges only after applying the update.

session-read-version.invariant: A session requires at least the version already observed or written and routes away from an older replica.

priority-queue.invariant: Priority metadata, with a stable sequence tie-breaker, changes which queued task is selected first.

delayed-queue.invariant: Eligibility depends on a not-before time, so a task remains delayed until the clock reaches its due time.

demand-backpressure.invariant: The producer advances only while downstream capacity is available; six tasks finish without buffering all six.

rate-window.invariant: A fixed time window admits at most two calls in each second.

timeout-boundary.invariant: A real asynchronous wait is cancelled by its timeout instead of remaining pending.

deadline-budget.invariant: The child inherits the remaining parent budget instead of starting an independent longer deadline.

subscription-fanout.invariant: Independent subscriptions each receive the two events, unlike one work queue that divides the two tasks.

event-payload.invariant: A notification identifies what changed; a carried-state event lets this consumer act without fetching the source.

consistent-ring.invariant: A hash ring assigns a key to its next virtual-node owner; adding D moves only the keys whose next owner becomes D.

transactional-inbox.invariant: A transaction records message consumption and its monetary effect together, with a unique message key.

cqrs-handlers.invariant: A command handler validates and updates the write model; a query handler reads a separate projection contract, which advances by events.

value-object.invariant: A monetary value compares by its components, rejects an invalid amount and is immutable without an entity identity.

message-translation.invariant: The translator creates the consumer schema and changes both field names and the amount unit.

read-through.invariant: The caller uses only cache.read; the cache API invokes its loader on a miss and stores the result.

oauth-code-pkce.invariant: The local authorization-code model binds verifier and redirect, permits one code redemption and issues an audience/scope-limited signed access token.

oidc-id-token-validation.invariant: The ID-token validation property checks issuer, audience, nonce, expiration and the configured HS256 signature before accepting the subject.

signed-key-rotation.invariant: A signed credential remains valid through the overlap and becomes inadmissible after its signing key is removed from trust.

signed-service-identity.invariant: The resource authenticates a signed service principal and validates its intended audience/scope rather than trusting a caller-supplied service label.

downscoped-token-exchange.invariant: The exchanged credential is bound to the target resource and a narrower delegated scope, preserving subject and actor identities.

verify-internal-request.invariant: Network location does not replace per-request identity and resource-policy verification in the tested boundary.

bastion-admin-hop.invariant: Administrative access is funneled through an authenticated jump boundary and direct access to the protected target is denied.

mutual-tls-peer-certs.invariant: Real SSLContext handshakes reject a client missing its certificate when mutual verification is required and authenticate both trusted peers before exchanging data.

distributed-cache-owner.invariant: Different logical workers use the same partition owner and share its populated cache entry, unlike independent per-worker caches.

paxos-accepted-carry.invariant: A prepare quorum reports accepted values; the proposer carries the value at the highest accepted ballot rather than inventing a different value.

raft-log-prefix.invariant: The follower checks the previous index/term before appending; a retry from a matching prefix replaces conflicting suffix entries.

election-one-vote.invariant: A voter remembers its vote in the term and refuses a second different candidate in that term.

three-phase-precommit.invariant: The extra precommit state distinguishes the modeled 3PC decision from an uncertain 2PC prepare, under the explicit timing and no-partition assumptions.

hybrid-clock-receive.invariant: The receive rule combines the physical maximum with a logical counter when the received wall component wins.

synchronous-replica-ack.invariant: The writer acknowledgement is ordered after this replica applies the write, providing the tested after-ack visibility property.

cascading-replication.invariant: Replication follows A to B to C, exposing the intermediate replica as the source of the final replica.

multi-writer-reconcile.invariant: Both sites accept writes and reconciliation preserves distinct additive credits instead of choosing one absolute snapshot.

standby-recovery-work.invariant: Standby readiness changes the restore/start/catch-up work required before the role transition.

automatic-failover-detection.invariant: A failure detector based on heartbeat age triggers the modeled role transition automatically.

failure-domain-spread.invariant: Replica placement across different failure domains leaves one instance after the declared zone or region outage.

golden-use-resource-signals.invariant: The sample distinguishes healthy process status from traffic/latency/errors/saturation and from resource utilization/saturation/errors.

opentelemetry-sdk-export.invariant: The real SDK exports two parent/child spans in one trace, propagates context and records one failed span for one request.

mvc-controller-model-view.invariant: The controller changes the model and selects a view; the view renders a DTO and never owns the write.

mvp-passive-view.invariant: The presenter loads and prepares the model result; a passive view only receives the display value.

mvvm-binding.invariant: A binding propagates an observable view-model property change into the view.

pac-agent-controls.invariant: Each agent owns abstraction, presentation and control; parent control coordinates the child agents.

inward-ports-and-layers.invariant: Ordered invocation exhibits layers; the domain depends on its port and two replaceable adapters implement that port, exhibiting the inward dependency property of Clean/Onion/Hexagonal designs.

module-public-contract.invariant: Public component contracts separate modules in one process; the order feature groups the steps of one vertical use case.

microkernel-plugin.invariant: A stable kernel invokes a registered extension through a shared contract.

blackboard-specialists.invariant: Independent specialists read and contribute to a shared problem state until their prerequisites become available.

actor-mailbox-writer.invariant: A private state owner serializes messages and provides a single writer for this actor.

event-driven-handler.invariant: The producer emits a fact and a subscribed handler reacts to it asynchronously in the local schedule.

service-boundaries.invariant: An explicit business service owns its store and operation contract; the other service failure does not mutate or prevent its operation in this controlled schedule.

serverless-invocation.invariant: The handler tolerates fresh invocation memory and keeps authoritative state outside that ephemeral environment.

space-based-grid.invariant: A partitioned memory grid owns data and co-locates processing; the same owner partitions can serve shared cache reads to different logical workers.

cell-failure-boundary.invariant: Independent cells contain one failure while the other cell completes its own request.

aggregate-root-invariant.invariant: The root owns the public mutation operation and checks the invariant spanning its children before accepting the next item.

domain-service-transfer.invariant: A domain operation involving two entities preserves the stated transfer invariant without belonging naturally to either entity alone.

repository-storage-contract.invariant: The repository presents a domain collection contract while storage representation changes behind it.

application-service-order.invariant: The application service coordinates the use case and calls domain behavior before persistence instead of embedding a write before validation.

domain-factory-validity.invariant: A factory centralizes the valid construction of the domain object and rejects invalid combinations.

specification-reuse.invariant: One named criterion is reused across selection and validation, eliminating the duplicated inconsistent predicate in this fixture.

context-contract-change.invariant: An actual schema change exposes affected consumers; bounded contexts give available different meanings, and the supplier/consumer agreement restores explicit contracts and a shared vocabulary within each context.

conformist-contract.invariant: The downstream deliberately adopts the upstream vocabulary and schema, including its coupling cost.

separate-ways-change.invariant: Choosing separate ways prevents an unrelated context from inheriting the other context change through a shared mutable object.

shared-kernel-impact.invariant: The shared kernel makes a small domain rule genuinely shared and exposes the joint impact of changing it.

open-host-service.invariant: A stable public service contract supports multiple consumers while internal representation changes behind it.

rest-resource-methods.invariant: Resource paths, method semantics and response status are explicit; GET does not become an operation that writes.

rpc-operation-contract.invariant: The dispatcher invokes an explicit operation and returns its result to the matching requester.

gateway-route-offload.invariant: The entry point routes requests, offloads authentication checks and forwards the accepted method/payload to the selected backend.

bff-composed-view.invariant: A server-side composition calls two owners and returns a client-specific view, reducing client round trips without pretending the backend calls disappear.

federated-entity-key.invariant: Entity-reference resolution joins fields owned by different subgraphs through the declared entity key instead of a display label.

hypermedia-affordance.invariant: The representation exposes state-dependent action links and the client follows an available relation rather than hardcoding every transition.

poll-vs-long-poll.invariant: Polling issues repeated requests; long polling holds one request until the result becomes available.

sse-event-resume.invariant: SSE event records carry IDs and data; a server can honor the last received ID when selecting the resumed stream.

websocket-duplex-frames.invariant: Two independent text-frame directions share the duplex model; client frames are masked and server frames are decoded without a new poll.

signed-webhook-callback.invariant: The provider pushes the event to a callback; signature verification precedes the receiver effect and the event identity suppresses a repeat.

sidecar-outbound-policy.invariant: A companion outbound proxy adds transport policy and identity; distributing the same policy to both companion proxies exhibits one mesh control/data-plane property.

tcc-resource-states.invariant: Try holds resources; Confirm consumes the hold, while Cancel releases the same held resources.

at-most-once-loss.invariant: At most one attempt avoids repeat delivery in this fixture but can lose the operation entirely.

cdc-committed-change.invariant: A database trigger captures only the committed after-image visible to the feed reader, allowing a destination to catch up instead of relying on a second independent application write.

outbox-cdc-feed.invariant: The transactional outbox is the captured table, and its committed insert becomes the CDC feed item.

bulkhead-independent-pools.invariant: A saturated dependency consumes only its own budget; the independent order pool retains capacity.

watchdog-restart.invariant: The supervisor detects the failed local state and rearms it through a replacement generation.

fallback-limited-function.invariant: The fallback preserves a deliberately reduced read function and labels the stale result instead of silently claiming full service.

chaos-delivery-experiment.invariant: A declared steady-state invariant is observed before/after an intentional fault and recovery experiment.

stream-offset-resume.invariant: An ordered event log and an explicit consumer position let the consumer resume the remaining events.

batch-stream-emission.invariant: Batch emits after the chosen finite input set completes; stream processing updates the result as each event arrives.

mapreduce-grouping.invariant: The map/group/reduce stages aggregate values per key instead of confusing all partial values with one total.

lambda-disjoint-views.invariant: Batch and speed-layer views cover disjoint input positions before being merged, preventing double counting at their boundary.

kappa-one-log-replay.invariant: One retained event log and one processing path support replay and ongoing processing rather than a separate batch algorithm.

choreographed-compensation.invariant: Local subscribers emit the next facts and a compensation handler reacts to the failure, exhibiting choreographed saga collaboration.

fire-forget-return.invariant: The caller does not await the later handler result, so its successful return does not prove eventual delivery or business completion.

fanin-source-correlation.invariant: Multiple input streams converge into one correlated output without discarding source ownership.

durable-workflow-resume.invariant: A persisted workflow identity and phase drive recovery after process-state loss, skipping the completed local step.

lease-expiry-owner.invariant: Expiry makes the abandoned authorization reclaimable, while owner comparison prevents an old owner from releasing the new lease.

shared-arbiter-lock.invariant: Both participants use one atomic unique-key arbiter instead of independent local locks; ownership is checked at release.

pessimistic-writer-lock.invariant: The writer obtains exclusion before changing the record; the second writer cannot begin its write transaction until release.

copy-on-write-snapshot.invariant: A writer changes a new copy instead of mutating the snapshot held by the old reader.

semaphore-permits.invariant: A real asyncio semaphore bounds concurrent entry to two and releases its permits after each task.

reused-thread-workers.invariant: The executor reuses two workers, forks four computations and joins their four results into one total.

idle-worker-steal.invariant: An idle worker steals eligible queued work from another worker while task ownership changes exactly once in this schedule.

reader-writer-exclusion.invariant: Concurrent readers are compatible with each other and incompatible with an exclusive writer in the finite state model.

spinlock-active-attempts.invariant: The contender repeatedly tests the lock state without blocking, consuming execution steps while the owner is paused.

cas-system-progress.invariant: The CAS retry pattern permits system progress while one contender stalls; this schedule also shows why that is not a per-thread bounded completion guarantee.

bounded-spsc-steps.invariant: With one producer, one consumer and atomic ordered index publication, each straight-line operation returns success/full/empty in at most four modeled steps without a retry loop.

reactive-demand-contract.invariant: Demand gates delivery and cancellation stops subsequent onNext-style emissions in this local publisher/subscriber contract.

rolling-recreate-capacity.invariant: Recreate produces a zero-ready interval in this schedule, while a one-at-a-time rolling replacement preserves one ready instance.

blue-green-route.invariant: Traffic changes between two already-provisioned environments and can return to the previous ready environment.

versioned-desired-reconcile.invariant: A versioned desired-state source drives the plan and reconciliation instead of allowing manual runtime drift to become the desired source.

immutable-replacement.invariant: The new infrastructure instance is created as a replacement while the prior instance remains unchanged.

strangler-abstraction-route.invariant: An abstraction preserves the caller contract while routing one extracted capability to its new owner, leaving the rest on the legacy path during transition.

decomposed-data-owners.invariant: Data is split into stores with explicit capability owners, exposing the need for an integration contract between the formerly shared consumers.

directory-shard.invariant: An explicit directory maps an entity key to its owning shard, independently of a hash function.

range-boundary.invariant: Half-open ranges assign the boundary key to exactly one shard rather than overlapping owners.

geographic-owner.invariant: A geographic attribute chooses the data owner rather than a key hash.

vertical-attributes.invariant: Vertical partitions divide attributes while preserving the key needed to reconstruct the logical entity.

log-structured-latest.invariant: Updates append records and reads resolve the latest version, exposing the read/compaction work introduced by a log-structured representation.

coalesced-snapshot-writes.invariant: Coalescing repeated overwrites of one snapshot reduces physical writes before the batch acknowledgement.

owner-latest-read.invariant: Every read in this single-owner schedule observes the latest preceding completed write, independently of a client session hint.

at-least-once-ack-retry.invariant: Retry after an ambiguous acknowledgement restores acknowledgement while admitting repeat delivery of the same event.
